# Where to Watch Not Cinderella’s Type


by Angel | September 17, 2026


What if finding love also meant discovering who you really are?


Indy has always believed her life with her aunt and uncle is fine. She keeps to herself, stays out of trouble, and doesn’t expect much to change. Then an accident brings Bryant Bailey into her life—and suddenly, everything she thought she knew starts to shift.


Based on the novel by Jenni James, *Not Cinderella’s Type* puts a fresh spin on a familiar story of unexpected love, self-worth, and finding where you belong.


[Stream Not Cinderella’s Type now on Angel.](https://www.angel.com/watch/not-cinderellas-type)


### **A Modern Cinderella Story**


The Cinderella story has been told countless ways, but *Not Cinderella’s Type* gives the familiar tale a contemporary setting and a different kind of heroine.


Indy isn’t waiting around for a prince to transform her life. She’s living the life she knows, even if she hasn’t stopped to question whether it’s really the life she wants.


Then Bryant enters the picture.


Their first meeting isn’t exactly romantic, and Bryant is about as far from Indy’s usual type as someone can be. Yet his persistence gradually breaks through the walls she’s built around herself, setting Indy on a journey she never expected to take.


### **Discovering Your Worth**


One of the most important parts of Indy’s story is learning that her value isn’t determined by the circumstances of her life.


For a long time, she accepts things as they are. But Bryant’s arrival forces her to look more closely at her relationships, her past, and the person she wants to become.


The journey isn’t about becoming someone else. It’s about discovering the person she already is—and recognizing that she deserves to be valued, respected, and loved.


That gives *Not Cinderella’s Type* a coming-of-age element alongside its romance, making Indy’s personal journey just as important as her relationship with Bryant.


### **Based on the Novel by Jenni James**


*Not Cinderella’s Type* is based on the novel by author Jenni James, bringing the story from the page to the screen.


For fans of the book, the adaptation offers a chance to see Indy and Bryant’s relationship play out visually. For audiences discovering the story for the first time, it stands on its own as a modern romance about two people who don’t necessarily expect to find each other.


One Rotten Tomatoes reviewer called the adaptation “fantastic,” while Angel Guild members praised the film as a strong choice for teens and families.


### **More Than a Fairy Tale**


While romance sits at the center of the story, *Not Cinderella’s Type* also explores themes that reach beyond relationships.


Indy’s experience touches on family, belonging, confidence, and the process of figuring out who you are. Bryant’s role in her life isn’t simply that of a love interest. He becomes someone who encourages her to recognize her own value and consider what she wants from the people around her.


That combination has made the movie appealing to viewers across generations. One Angel Guild member called it “a great movie for teens” and said it kept her attention at 60, describing it as a movie for the whole family.


### **Watch** ***Not Cinderella’s Type*** **on Angel**


*Not Cinderella’s Type* offers a fresh take on the Cinderella story—one where finding love is only part of the adventure.
